plan.title: AD treated vs control: Salmon→tximport→DESeq2 DE
plan.analytical_narrative: The inputs are 12 per-sample Salmon quant.sf directories (30,147 transcripts each) plus a transcript-to-gene map — no gene-level count matrix. The correct path for that data state is tximport summarization to gene level with the average-transcript-length offset (protects against differential isoform use), followed by DESeq2's negative binomial Wald test for the 6 treated vs 6 control contrast. A minimal pre-filter, median-of-ratios size factors, independent filtering with BH at alpha 0.05, and apeglm shrinkage of the reported fold change complete the primary inference. Because both groups have 6 replicates — the low end where DE tools disagree most — an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test runs on the same imported counts as a robustness check, and the report treats the intersection as the high-confidence gene set. Sample-structure QC (blind vst, PCA, distance heatmap) runs before any test to catch outliers in skin biopsies, where inter-donor variance is large. The research question names no fold-change threshold, so genes are selected on adjusted p-value alone (zero-null test), with shrunken log2FC for ranking and display only.

steps.method: tximport gene-level import with average transcript length offset, then blind vst, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap
DESeq2 Wald test
apeglm shrinkage of log2 fold change
Benjamini-Hochberg with independent filtering
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test (robustness check on the same tximport counts, report overlap with DESeq2)
DE report: MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram, gene table with unshrunken and shrunken log2FC and lfcSE, ranked by shrunken log2FC, padj < 0.05, DESeq2/edgeR overlap, session info
